Portfolio news brief — 3 September 2026

Market and major-name developments
- Treasury yields moved lower across the curve on Thursday, as traders reacted to remarks by Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller saying he's leaning toward keeping interest rates unchanged at the central bank's next policy meeting in two weeks. The 10-year Treasury note yield, the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt, fell more than 4 basis points to 4.748%. (CNBC)
- Treasury Department is very worried about long-term yields on government bonds. That's because rising yields are a huge headache for Uncle Sam. (The Motley Fool)
- Joyce Chang, Chair of Global Research at JPMorgan, says deficits and sticky inflation could push yields higher and make a Fed hike the next move, while global growth broadens. (CNBC)
- Japanese public company Remixpoint sold all its Ethereum , Solana , XRP, and Dogecoin on Sept. 1, making Bitcoin the only cryptocurrency left in its treasury. (Decrypt)
- NuScale Power ( SMR +1.15% ) is a popular nuclear energy stock with significant upside potential. The company is valued at just $4 billion despite operating in what could become a $300 billion global market. (The Motley Fool)

Meta (META)
- Meta has agreed to pay up to $17 billion and make sweeping changes to Instagram and Facebook as part of a landmark settlement with nearly every U.S. The deal introduces new protections for teens, but implementing those safeguards, particularly determining users’ ages, presents major challenges. (CNBC)
- In what is being referred to as potentially social media's "Big Tobacco moment," Meta Platforms ( META +3.48% ) recently announced an agreement with 52 attorneys general under which the parent company of Facebook and Instagram will pay up to $18 billion over the next decade and significantly change its policies for teen users. While the fine would be the largest consumer-protection settlement ever, excluding Big Tobacco, most Wall Street analysts and experts believe Meta avoided what could have been a vastly larger (The Motley Fool)

SanDisk (SNDK)
- Sandisk ( SNDK +1.14% ) built its name on memory cards and flash drives. But in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, which ended July 3, the company sold $2.98 billion of storage to datacenter customers -- about a third of its $8.97 billion in total revenue . (The Motley Fool)

NVIDIA (NVDA; VOO top-five holding)
- Nvidia has officially agreed to buy open-source artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, as the chipmaker moves beyond hardware and further up the AI stack. With the deal, which has been expected since The Information reported on it last week, Hugging Face will "remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a blog post Thursday. (CNBC)
- Here are the biggest calls on Wall Street on Thursday. (CNBC)
- Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue join 'Squawk Box' to discuss Nvidia's deal to acquire Hugging Face for for $12.9 billion, how the deal came about, the importance of open models, and more. (CNBC)

Bitcoin (BTC)
- US spot Ethereum and XRP ETFs broke their winning streaks on Wednesday. Bitcoin funds went the other way, pulling in $101.15 million in fresh money, per SoSoValue and Decrypt data. (Decrypt)
- The crypto market—including Bitcoin and altcoins like XRP , Ethereum , and BNB—is riding a bullish wave of momentum in the U.S. stock market, seemingly triggered by fresh comments from the Federal Reserve, and sending short sellers to goblintown. (Decrypt)

Eli Lilly (LLY; XLV top-five holding)
- This week, Eli Lilly ( LLY -0.02% ) announced a deal that will add to its already formidable drug pipeline. The drug maker said it will acquire Merida Biosciences for $2.9 billion, beefing up its pipeline of potential treatments for autoimmune and allergic diseases. (The Motley Fool)

Apple (AAPL; VOO top-five holding)
- This year has seen its fair share of major leadership transitions. After more than half a century at the helm, Berkshire Hathaway 's Warren Buffett retired as CEO on Dec. (The Motley Fool)

Microsoft (MSFT; VOO top-five holding)
- Microsoft's Xbox unit said Thursday that it will impose monthly cloud gaming time limits for Game Pass subscribers after years of unlimited access, as the company seeks to find a better balance between usage and costs. Players will be able to pay for additional hours beyond the caps, which go into effect in November. (CNBC)
- Microsoft will start disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business for the first time, providing investors with a clearer picture of its business that competes with Amazon Web Services and Google's cloud platform. The change, announced in a presentation on Wednesday, is part of a broader shift in Microsoft's reporting structure, as the company trims its operating segments from three to two. (CNBC)
- Microsoft ( MSFT +3.23% ) continues to deliver exceptional quarterly results, with cloud computing playing a major role. Not only was cloud revenue up by 27% year over year in its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, but that growth came along with sales backlog growth of 84% year-over-year to $678 billion. (The Motley Fool)

Alphabet (GOOGL; VOO top-five holding)
- After wrapping up its longest monthly losing streak on Wall Street in more than a decade, Google has started September by giving investors several reasons for optimism. The company on Wednesday launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks, alongside a new cybersecurity model aimed at trusted government and enterprise customers. (CNBC)
- Broadcom could see a lot of upside, even as investors seem to express doubts over its business outside of its Google partnership, per Macquarie Equity Research. (CNBC)

Informational only — verify primary sources before making investment decisions.
Routine price moves and stock-picking speculation are intentionally excluded.
